title: Yosef Mokir Shabbei, Who Honored Shabbat

paragraphs: Yosef Mokir Shabbei—Yosef who honored Shabbat.

Shabbat 119a relates that he received this name because he greatly honored Shabbat. His gentile neighbor was told by astrologers that all his property would eventually come to Yosef. He sold everything, bought one pearl and hid it in his hat. While he was crossing by ferry, the wind blew it into the water and a fish swallowed it. The fish was caught and brought to market at twilight on Shabbat eve. No one would buy it, but Yosef Mokir Shabbata did. When he cut it open, he found the pearl and sold it for thirteen lofts of gold dinars. An old man met him and said: “Whoever lends to Shabbat, Shabbat repays.”

notes.text: Shabbei is itself attested in the checked account and means that he honored Shabbat. “Thirteen lofts of gold dinars” preserves the account’s expression for the price, rather than making up a modern monetary equivalent.

The consulted Shabbat 119a directly has Yosef Mokar Shabbei, the ferry, pearl, fish and thirteen lofts of gold dinars. The supplied heading and price expression remain without a modern valuation or silent heading correction; historical provisional-title statements remain in their versions.
